title: Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB) - Current Rate
summary: The Interest on Reserve Balances (IORB) rate is currently 3.65% as of April 20, 2026, unchanged from the prior observation on April 19. The rate has remained flat at 3.65% for the five-day period from April 16 through April 20.
key_points: Rate has been stable at 3.65% from April 16-20, 2026
IORB is the interest rate the Federal Reserve pays on reserve balances held by depository institutions
why_it_matters: IORB serves as the floor for the federal funds rate in the current monetary policy implementation framework. The 3.65% rate level is consistent with the top of the Federal Open Market Committee's target range for the federal funds rate. Changes to IORB can signal shifts in the Fed's monetary policy stance or implementation adjustments.
macro_context: IORB is the interest rate the Federal Reserve pays on reserve balances held by depository institutions at Federal Reserve Banks. It is a key administrative rate set by the Federal Reserve as part of its monetary policy implementation framework, typically positioned at or just below the top of the FOMC's federal funds rate target range.
market_structure_context: IORB is a critical rate in the Federal Reserve's framework for implementing monetary policy, serving as the primary mechanism through which the Fed influences short-term interest rates in the banking system.
